record.paper_title: Selected results and open problems in a semiclassical theory of dense matter
record.original_question: In the Savic-Kasanin (SK) semiclassical theory of dense matter, the mean density rho of a planetary body is related to the mean solar density rho_0 by rho = rho_0 2^phi. A modern re-check using densities of 22 planets and major satellites reportedly still supports this relation, but now with non-integral values of the exponent phi for some objects. What physical interpretation, if any, should be assigned to these non-integral values of phi, and can they be explained by a principled extension of the earlier interpretation that treated integral phi values as a qualitative analogy to atomic quantization and pressure-induced changes in atomic structure?

evidence.quote: It was shown that eq.(1) is still valid,but that the exponent phi can also take non-integral values. The immediate question is of course the interpretation of these non-integral values.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following empirical density law for planetary bodies in the Solar System. Let $\rho_0$ denote the mean density of the Sun, and for each planet or major satellite let $\rho$ denote its mean density. Postulate the relation
$$\rho = \rho_0 \cdot 2^{\varphi},$$
where $\varphi \in \mathbb{R}$ is an exponent assigned to that body. In the original semiclassical framework in which this law was proposed, integral values $\varphi \in \mathbb{Z}$ were interpreted qualitatively as a discrete quantization analogous to atomic shell quantization and pressure-induced changes in atomic structure under self-gravity.

A modern recomputation using the measured mean densities of a sample of 22 planets and major satellites confirms the relation in the sense that each body can be assigned a value of $\varphi$, but the resulting exponents are generally non-integral, $\varphi \notin \mathbb{Z}$.

Problem: Provide a principled physical interpretation of the non-integral values of $\varphi$ in this density law, and decide whether such non-integral exponents can be derived as a natural extension of the original "discrete-quantization" interpretation (e.g., from a continuous family of intermediate compressed atomic/electronic configurations under planetary pressure) rather than being merely an empirical fit parameter.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open interpretive problem within the Savić-Kašanin semiclassical theory of dense matter. Web searches turn up the original sources and later applications of the theory (to Galilean satellites, metallization pressures, and fluid structure via a unified Bošković-Savić-Kašanin framework), but no source provides a definitive physical interpretation of the non-integral exponents in the $\rho = \rho_0 \, 2^{\varphi}$ law. The status therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.snippet: The exponent phi can also take non-integral values. The immediate question is of course the interpretation of these non-integral values.
status_evidence.claim: The interpretation of non-integral phi is explicitly listed as an open question.

status_evidence.title: Supermolecular structure and phase state of fluid based on the unified Bošković-Savić-Kašanin theory
status_evidence.snippet: Unified Bošković-Savić-Kašanin theory applied to fluids.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work extends the SK theory but does not resolve the interpretation of non-integral phi in the planetary density relation.
